storytelling_moments.summary: Two lovers enter the cabin and have sex while the camera moves outside.
A camera move connects the cabin to a parked Plymouth in the woods.
A drunk Andy watches the cabin, loads a revolver, and leaves his car.
Andy approaches the lovers but stops on the path, devastated, with the gun at his side.
Under questioning, Andy admits the quarrel and gun but denies the murders; the prosecutor challenges his account.
The prosecutor presents circumstantial evidence and argues that eight shots imply deliberate reloading.
Jurors eat dinner while returning guilty votes.
The judge sentences Andy to consecutive life terms; the opening titles conclude.
Red claims rehabilitation after twenty years; the parole board rejects him.
Red introduces his prison supply business as inmates gather to watch the new arrivals.
Andy rides through the gates in chains while Red narrates his conviction and former profession.
Hadley strikes Andy; Red and the other inmates bet on which newcomer will break first.
Norton imposes religious discipline and Hadley terrorizes the newcomers through admission and delousing.
New inmates undergo an invasive medical examination.
Naked newcomers attend a compulsory Bible reading.
The men enter Cellblock Five; Red describes first-night terror and his wager on Andy.
Andy is locked alone in his cell and begins to dress.
The prison exterior and a passing train establish the first night.
Red waits in his cell and listens to approaching footsteps.
Lights go out; inmates taunt the new arrivals while Red waits for a breakdown.
A montage of newcomers shows several different reactions to confinement.
Red listens for Andy while Heywood begins targeting another prisoner.
Heywood taunts the crying newcomer, who finally screams that he wants to go home.
Heywood celebrates winning his bet.
Hadley brutally beats the distressed newcomer, then has him carried to the infirmary.
Red watches the blood below and recalls that Andy never made a sound.
Morning count finds Andy neatly dressed as Red studies him.
At breakfast Brooks feeds Jake, Heywood collects his winnings, and Tyrell reports the newcomer died; Andy asks his name.
Bob introduces Andy to difficult laundry work.
Bogs, Rooster and Pete intimidate Andy in the showers.
Andy lies awake in his cell.
Andy approaches Red, counters Heywood’s baseball intimidation, and negotiates for a rock hammer while Red warns him about prison risks.
Andy discreetly passes Red the payment.
Red unfolds the payment in his cell.
Leonard and a truck driver coordinate a package delivery through the laundry dock.
Leonard removes and conceals the package while sorting laundry.
Leonard transfers the package to Red through clean laundry in exchange for cigarettes.
Red opens the rock hammer and laughs at how implausible escape with it seems.
Brooks delivers the tool to Andy and carries back a note through his book-cart route.
Red opens Andy’s handwritten thank-you.
Bob sends Andy from the laundry line to fetch Hexlite.
The Sisters overpower and sexually assault Andy in the stock area; the camera retreats to the laundry line.
A 1947–1949 montage combines prison routine, rock work, recurring assaults and resistance.
Andy sits injured in solitary while Red describes the punishment.
Red describes the first two years as nearly destructive while Andy works the laundry.
Norton announces a roof-resurfacing detail and solicits volunteers.
Prisoners enter their names; Red privately approaches Youngblood.
Youngblood selects Red, Andy and their associates for the detail.
Red pays Youngblood in cigarettes for the selected places.
A bucket of hot tar is hoisted from the factory exterior toward the roof.
On the roof, Andy hears Hadley’s inheritance complaint, risks approaching him, and offers financial help in exchange for beer for the crew.
A cooler of beer follows the tar bucket’s route up the building.
The crew drinks in the sun; Andy quietly watches and declines a beer as Red offers possible interpretations of his gesture.

relations.rationale: Red’s wager on Andy is later lost when Andy makes no sound.
The prisoner’s audible breakdown brings the guards and Hadley’s response.
Tyrell reports the beaten man’s death; it is not shown as a death on screen.
Red sees the small tool and understands Andy’s earlier joke.
Delivery brings a handwritten thank-you back to Red.
Fetching supplies takes Andy into the stock area where the Sisters wait.
The later cigarette payment explains the selected roofing positions.
The tar-bucket hoist is repeated by the beer-cooler hoist.
The offered financial work secures the beer the crew drinks afterward.

review_issues.description: Working editorial boundary: ends before the checkers scene on printed page 37. Grounded in the saved Act I rooftop analysis; not an explicitly saved Act boundary.
Text is preserved relative to pdftotext extraction, not certified as a lossless PDF transcription. Visual inspection covered the boundary page; the remaining pages need transcription QA.
Printed pages 21–22 join action to dialogue on the same indented lines (Red glances at the hand; Red gives Andy a look). Raw text retained; automatic block typing needs correction against PDF layout.
The indented song lyric has no character cue and is retained as unattributed_text, not assigned to Andy.
